## Natural history notes

A slender twig ant characterized by its long narrow body, large eyes, long legs, and orange-brown to dark brown coloration. In Florida, it is found in trees, shrubs, gardens, forest edges, hammocks, parks, and other wooded or landscaped habitats where it forages along branches, trunks, vines, and vegetation. It nests in hollow twigs, stems, dead branches, or cavities, and feeds on small insects, nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources while moving quickly and aggressively when disturbed.
